papers.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

papers.title: Magnetar driven Dainotti relation with up to 56\% reduced uncertainties: probing the Expansion History of the Universe
papers.abstract: The persistent tension in Hubble constant measurements and recent DESI hints of dynamical dark energy motivate extending the distance ladder beyond Type~Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) and Cosmic Chronometers (CC) into the largely unexplored range $z\sim2$--$6$. We use X-ray plateau emission of long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), standardized through the two-dimensional Dainotti relation, as a probe of this gap. We analyze two samples: a platinum sample (P50, 50~GRBs, light-curve quality cuts) and a magnetar sample (M23, 23~GRBs, selected by requiring the magnetar spin-down model to be statistically preferred over the Willingale parametrization). We calibrate the Dainotti relation anchored independently to the Master SNe~Ia compilation and to Cosmic Chronometers, and propagate the result into a joint flat-$\Lambda$CDM inference via MCMC. Despite containing less than half the GRBs of P50, M23 yields an intrinsic scatter $\sim41\%$ smaller, demonstrating that physically motivated selection outperforms quality cuts. Both samples give nearly identical cosmological constraints once combined with SNe~Ia and CC: M23 gives $H_0=69.45\pm0.32\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\Omega_m=0.34^{+0.01}_{-0.02}$; P50 gives $H_0=69.46\pm0.33$ and $\Omega_m=0.34\pm0.02$, both in $3$--$3.5\sigma$ tension with Planck and SH0ES. We further introduce a novel joint likelihood that simultaneously fits individual plateau light curves and the Dainotti correlation, reducing the intrinsic scatter by $\sim56\%$ relative to the platinum sample and avoiding local maxima from sparse light-curve data. These results establish magnetar-selected GRB plateaus as a robust, high-redshift complement to existing distance-ladder probes, with a clear path toward improved constraining efficiency as sample sizes grow.

papers.title: TeV Gamma-Ray Transparency Bounds on Neutrinos and Axions
papers.abstract: Multi-TeV gamma rays propagating over cosmological distances measure the extragalactic background light (EBL) through attenuation by electron--positron pair production. This is particularly valuable in the infrared, where the EBL is difficult to measure directly. Since the growing sample of observed multi-TeV photons provides tight constraints on the EBL photon intensity, this, in turn, constrains new particles that radiatively decay into meV--eV photons. We set the first TeV-transparency bounds on active-neutrino electromagnetic transition moments, obtain new constraints on radiatively decaying sterile neutrinos, and derive competitive limits on the axion--photon coupling.

papers.title: Tidally Induced Coda: Double Transients from Black Hole-Star Binary Encounters with Massive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (MBHs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. In particular, the tidal field of an MBH can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. Here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (BH) and a star. Using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code SpaceHub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between BH-star binaries and MBHs. We systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and MBH mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($\mu$TDE), as the star is disrupted by its BH companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the MBH. We derive fitting formulae for the $\mu$TDE cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an MBH of $10^6\,M_\odot$. These double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $\mu$TDEs. We estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm Gpc}$.

papers.title: Probing the X-Ray Structure of the $z = 2.38$ Strongly Lensed Quasar J1721+8842, the First Einstein Zig-Zag Lens, Down to $140\ \mathrm{pc}$
papers.abstract: Sub-kiloparsec X-ray structures in active galactic nuclei (AGN), including outflows, jets, and dual AGN, provide key insights into their evolution and influence on host galaxies. In the local universe, Chandra X-ray Observatory's state-of-the-art $0.5''$ angular resolution has resolved these structures, but at $z > 0.1$, milliarcsecond resolution is required to spatially resolve sub-kpc scales. We leverage the spatial amplification by strong gravitational lensing to investigate the X-ray structure of J1721+8842, a $z=2.38$ quasar lensed into six images. To reconstruct the optical emission position, we model the lensing mass distribution using the six quasar images, five detected by Gaia Data Release 3 (A-E) and one by HST (F). Our model reproduces the five Gaia image positions to milliarcsecond precision. To locate the X-ray emission relative to the optical, we combine ray-trace simulations of archival Chandra observations with the lens model image position predictions using a double maximum-likelihood analysis. We constrain the X-ray centroid within a $0.017''\times0.004''\ (139\times30\ \mathrm{pc})$ ellipse centered $0.005''\ (44\ \mathrm{pc})$ away from the optical source position. Source-plane reconstructions of the soft-X-ray and hard-X-ray to optical sources demonstrate these emission regions are cospatial, allowing the optical source at $1\sigma$ confidence. These results indicate no evidence for kpc-scale X-ray jets, outflows, or dual AGN with projected separations exceeding $140\ \mathrm{pc}$. This method improves Chandra's effective angular resolution by a factor of 30 at cosmological distances, enabling studies of sub-kpc AGN X-ray structure at cosmic noon.

papers.title: Constraining the Leptonic and Hadronic Contributions to the Gamma-Ray Emission of SNR HESS J1731-347 with CTAO Forecasts
papers.abstract: We present a Bayesian broadband spectral analysis of the supernova remnant HESS J1731-347, combining archival radio, X-ray, and H.E.S.S. data with a new analysis of 16 yr of Fermi-LAT observations. The LAT data allow the GeV emission of the western molecular-cloud core (MC-core) to be separated from that of the remaining shell. We fit purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models with and without the MC-core region. Within a one-zone model with fixed distance and ambient density, the lepto-hadronic scenario is strongly preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) in both cases. Excluding the MC-core, we obtain $\Delta{\rm BIC}=33.67$, a magnetic field of $B = 84.9^{+27.5}_{-22.9}$ $\mu$G, a hard proton index of $\alpha_p = 1.69 \pm 0.10$, and a proton energy of $W_p = (4.37^{+0.64}_{-0.51})\times10^{48}$ erg for $n_{\rm H}=20$ cm$^{-3}$. The preference for a hadronic contribution is therefore not driven by the MC-core emission alone. CTAO simulations show that a 50 h observation with the southern array would detect the source at $13\sigma$ to $18\sigma$ and substantially improve the constraints on its TeV spectrum.

papers.title: Elastic polar oscillations and nuclear parameters
papers.abstract: Owing to the elasticity of a neutron star, the shear and interface modes are excited, in addition to the fundamental, pressure, and gravity modes. While direct observations of the oscillation spectrum remain challenging, potential resonance signatures from these modes could be manifested in the precursors of short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron star mergers. If the oscillation spectrum is observed, this is a good opportunity to extract the physical properties through the technique of asteroseismology. In particular, we focus on the crustal elasticity and examine the $s$- and $i$-mode frequencies. We find that, for a given EOS specified by the nuclear saturation parameters, the radius-scaled $s$-mode frequencies and the mass-scaled $i$-mode frequencies can be expressed as a function of the stellar compactness, independently of the stiffness of the core EOS, at least when the EOS in a higher-density region can be characterized only by the specific constant sound velocity. Then, we could derive the fitting formula for the $s_i$-mode for $i=1-4$ and $i_1$-mode frequencies as a function of the stellar compactness and the combination of the incompressibility of symmetric nuclear matter, $K_0$, and the slope parameter for the nuclear symmetry energy, $L$. If the $s$- and/or $i$-mode oscillation frequencies were observed, one may get the relation between these properties by identifying the observed frequencies with specific modes, using our fitting formula, which offers useful insights into the nuclear saturation parameters and stellar properties. By combining the other observational data, it may be possible to narrow the parameter space of EOS parameters and stellar properties. We emphasize that this article summarizes the results presented in our previous studies and discusses their implications for neutron star seismology.

papers.title: Phase-Resolved X-ray Polarimetry of LMC X-1: Enhanced Polarization at Inferior Conjunction
papers.abstract: We present a phase-resolved X-ray polarimetric analysis of the extragalactic black hole X-ray binary LMC X-1, a classical high/soft state source with a well-characterized accretion disk and an ionization cone/inferred jet. Previous X-ray polarimetry gave only orbit-averaged upper limits on the polarization fraction, leaving any orbital-phase dependence unexplored. We aim to probe how this polarization depends on orbital phase and to identify the origin of the polarized emission. We analyzed simultaneous IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR observations taken in October 2022. We measured the polarization degree and angle in different energy bands as a function of orbital phase, performed spectro-polarimetric modeling to identify the emitting components, and modeled the phase modulation of the Stokes parameters with a cosine function. The polarization depends on orbital phase: during inferior conjunction (phase from -0.1 to 0.1), the polarization degree is (4.2+/-1.1)% in 2-3 keV and (3.4+/-0.8)% in 2-8 keV, with polarization angles of (46+/-8) and (50+/-7) degrees. Outside this phase it stays below the 99% minimum detectable polarization. The measured angle agrees with the ionization cone/jet direction (~45 degrees), and spectro-polarimetric modeling favors a soft-band origin for the polarization. The Stokes Q/I and U/I modulation is well described by a cosine at the orbital period and favors two spatially separated polarized components over a single one varying in amplitude. We also tested whether differential Faraday rotation of the disk light in an ordered magnetic field can reproduce the modulation and used it to place upper limits on the magnetic field. These results show that soft-band polarization of LMC X-1 appears only near inferior conjunction at a position angle aligned with the disk normal, and highlight the importance of orbital-phase sampling in polarimetric studies.

papers.title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
papers.abstract: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

papers.title: Critical Eddington luminosity and photon cooling of compact spherical stars
papers.abstract: Context. Relativistic corrections to the luminosity have been used for neutron stars of radius greater than $3MG/c^2$ in studies of X-ray bursts. However, there is no fundamental limit that excludes the existence of more compact massive objects with a physical surface, fluid or solid. Aims. We aim to discuss critical "Eddington" luminosity for spherical stars that have a surface within the sphere of unstable circular photon orbits (photon sphere). Methods. We use standard analytical ray-tracing formulae in the Schwarzschild metric. Results. We find that for stars within the photon sphere, the Eddington condition for balance between radiative force and gravitational attraction is fundamentally altered by photons returning to the surface. The equilibrium is non-local and requires stationarity on timescales of photon fall-back. As a result, spontaneous symmetry breaking is possible, leading to non-uniformity of emission across the photospheric surface. Conclusions. For a fixed intrinsic luminosity, the photons returning to the surface decrease the cooling rate of stars inside their photon sphere. At the same time, the returning photons increase the value of the critical luminosity that would balance gravity. One and the same redshifted formula applies to the critical luminosity, as seen by a distant observer, for any radius of the star. In the X-ray burst literature, for stars with radius less than 3 gravitational radii a different formula has long been accepted that missed the essential physics of the photons emitted in directions outside the escape cone.

papers.title: Cosmic ray protons from 40 GeV to 10 EeV due to star formation?
papers.abstract: The formation of massive stars eventually results in supernovae explosions. Typical supernova remnants (SNRs) accelerate cosmic ray (CR) protons up to $E_{max-p} \sim 10$ TeV; the value of $E_{max-p}$ may reach $\sim 1$ EeV for the case of the hypernovae and/or for a sub-relativistic velocity of the SNR's shock wave. We show that the observable CR proton spectrum in the energy range between 40 GeV and 10 EeV is reasonably well described with a sum of three components that correspond to three distinct SNR populations. We consider two basic scenarios of CR origin: I) the supergalactic scenario assuming diffusion of the protons inside a magnetic field structure with the characteristic radius $H = 1-20$ Mpc and II. the cosmological scenario with the maximum redshift of the sources $z_{max} = 6$.

papers.title: Stellar-evolution systematic biases on $^{12}\text{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\text{O}$ constraints from the primordial-black-hole mass gap
papers.abstract: The $^{12}\text{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\text{O}$ reaction determines helium-burning carbon-oxygen core masses and sets the pair-instability-supernova mass-gap boundary, which limits the maximum mass of stellar-origin primordial black holes. Gravitational-wave population analyses using GWTC-4 report a low-spin-black-hole upper cutoff at $68.5^{+19.8}_{-18.5}\,M_\odot$, implying a low astrophysical S-factor $S_{300}\approx 108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$, in tension with canonical nuclear-astrophysics evaluations. However, stellar-evolution systematic uncertainties from metallicity, rotation, and mass-loss prescriptions remain poorly quantified. Here we use the MESA stellar-evolution code to construct a three-dimensional parameter grid disentangling these coupled effects. We show that metallicity-dependent winds dominate helium-core retention; rotation suppresses carbon consumption via centrifugal cooling and meridional mixing; different mass-loss prescriptions produce $8$-$10\,M_\odot$ offsets in the black-hole-mass-gap edge. A parameter combination $Z\approx10^{-3}$, moderate rotation $\omega/\omega_\mathrm{crit}=0.4$, and optically-thin C15 winds reproduces the GWTC-4 inferred maximum primordial-black-hole mass for $S_{300}=108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$. The canonical $45\,M_\odot$ gap boundary represents an overlapping statistical intersection of black-hole-population distributions rather than a universal physical threshold. Our framework provides a pathway to jointly constrain nuclear-reaction rates, stellar-evolution physics, and gravitational-wave-source populations.

papers.title: MINDS: The mid-infrared spectrum of the disk, jets, and winds of DG Tau
papers.abstract: DG Tau is one of the best-studied young stellar objects in transition from a Class I protostar to a T Tauri star. It is no longer embedded in a dense molecular cloud, but still reveals features that are commonly seen in protostars at earlier evolutionary stages. DG Tau hosts a protoplanetary disk and two energetic jets that can be studied down to the immediate environment of the star and disk at optical, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths. We use the Medium Resolution Spectrometer of MIRI on the James Webb Space Telescope. DG Tau's mid-infrared spectrum consists of a very bright continuum with various silicate features, and lines of CO, H$_2$O, OH, H I, H$_2$, Ne$^{+}$, Ne$^{2+}$, Ar$^{+}$, Fe$^{+}$, and Ni$^{+}$. We find substantial grain growth to at least 2 $\mu$m at an early evolutionary stage. Lines of H$_2$O and CO are formed at extremely high temperatures (600-2000 K). The ratio of warm to hot water is the lowest among previous observations of disks with JWST. This and a very strong continuum point toward the relevance of the strong accretion of DG Tau and consequently strong stellar UV irradiation. The pair of jets reveals a rich spectrum of emission lines from ions, in particular producing forbidden lines of [Ne II], [Ne III], [Ar II], [Fe II], and [Ni II]. The forward jet shows a collimated structure as found previously, while the hitherto poorly described, receding jet is more widely dispersed on scales of several arcsec, showing a layered structure with the fastest components being the most collimated. The ionization of the jet gas cannot be reconciled with high-energy radiation from the star itself. Instead, we propose a unified nonequilibrium ionization shock model in which the previously studied X-ray jet plasma continuously cools, recombining ions until, at temperatures around $10^4$ K and below, metals at low ionization stages emit the observed ion lines.

papers.title: Super-Eddington Neutron Star Accretion Columns: Comparing GRRMHD Simulations with Spectral Models
papers.abstract: The geometry and structure of neutron star accretion columns affect the X-ray emission in super-Eddington accreting systems. We perform four axisymmetric general relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations of super-Eddington accretion onto magnetized neutron stars with the maximum surface magnetic fields ranging from $3\times10^{10}$ to $1\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{G}$. We measure the column width and estimate the characteristic radiation shock heights from the flow velocity and velocity gradient. Across the four models, the angular width decreases from approximately $0.14$ to $0.07\,\mathrm{rad}$, while the estimated shock height increases from $1.95$ to $3.89\,\mathrm{km}$. We then compare our solutions to the best-fit values derived from spectral modeling of super-Eddington Be/X-ray binary outbursts. We calculate area-equivalent column radii that vary between 5.2 and 3.2 km, three of which fall within the upper part of the range inferred from spectral results using the \texttt{bwcycl} model.

papers.title: On the potential of widening the band of X-ray polarimetry
papers.abstract: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has made X-ray polarimetry a routine astrophysical diagnostic, but its sensitivity is confined to the 2-8 keV band, where the photoelectric effect in a gas is most efficiently exploited. Several of the questions raised by its results, as well as some classical goals of high-energy astrophysics, require polarimetry below 2~keV, to reach the thermal emission of neutron stars, black-hole discs and blazars, and above 8~keV, where reflection, cyclotron lines and the non-thermal emission of supernova remnants, pulsar wind nebulae and magnetars can be isolated. Following a recent review of the subject, we discuss the scientific case for extending the band over roughly 0.1-80 keV and beyond, and the techniques that can deliver it: Bragg diffraction on graded multilayers, photoelectric gas imagers read out by pixel ASICs with time-of-arrival capability, time projection chambers and focal-plane Compton polarimeters, including their combination in stacked focal planes. We then summarise how these techniques are being implemented, or could be, in REDSoX and GOSoX, eXTP, XPP, WXPT and in EXPO and PHEMTO, proposed to the ESA M8 call, as well as in the wide-field transient polarimeter POLAR-2, and we discuss the trade-offs that will drive the design of a wide-band polarimetry mission.

papers.title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
papers.abstract: Superfluids, in a spinning-down container with pinning centres, exhibit sudden collective migration of quantized vortices. The onset, progress, and termination of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we show that: 1) the first exodus of vortices occurs when a sector of the vortex array, having a minimum opening angle, is vacated close to the wall; 2) driven by this exodus, the superfluid flow near the boundary continually decreases in strength and arrests the exit; and 3) the resultant depletion region has well-defined dimensions---governed primarily by the critical unpinning velocity, the container size, and the initial rotation rate---that limit the angular momentum transferred to the container. We conclude by discussing the relevance to pulsar glitches.

papers.title: $\Phi$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
papers.abstract: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $\Phi$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $\Phi$-Stages, each augmented by a $\Phi$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $\Phi$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $\rho>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $\rho\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

papers.title: On the evidence of lensing in GW231123
papers.abstract: Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. The lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. A comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}\sigma$. This makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.

papers.title: Investigating tidal heating in neutron stars via gravitational Raman scattering
papers.abstract: We present a scattering amplitude formalism to study the tidal heating effects of nonspinning neutron stars incorporating both worldline effective field theory and relativistic stellar perturbation theory. In neutron stars, tidal heating arises from fluid viscosity due to various scattering processes in the interior. It also serves as a channel for the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the neutron star and its environment. In the interior of the neutron star, we first derive two master perturbation equations that capture fluid perturbations accurate to linear order in frequency. Remarkably, these equations receive no contribution from bulk viscosity due to a peculiar adiabatic incompressibility which arises in stellar fluid for non-barotropic perturbations. In the exterior, the metric perturbations reduce to the Regge-Wheeler (RW) equation which we solve using the analytical Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi (MST) method. We compute the amplitude for gravitational waves scattering off a neutron star, also known as gravitational Raman scattering. From the amplitude, we obtain expressions for the electric quadrupolar static Love number and the leading dissipation number to all orders in compactness. We then compute the leading dissipation number for various realistic equation-of-state(s) and estimate the change in the number of gravitational wave cycles due to tidal heating during inspiral in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) band. We find that the shear-viscous contribution is small. Even for cold ($T\sim 10^5$K) and weakly compact stars it changes the number of cycles by less than $10^{-2}$, about an order of magnitude below the other conservative 4PN contributions, and it decreases as $T^{-2}$ for hotter stars.

papers.title: Spiral Density Waves and Torque Balance in the Kerr Geometry
papers.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in relativistic accretion discs are a key science target for the upcoming LISA mission. Existing models of disc-EMRI interactions typically rely on crude dynamical friction or Newtonian planetary migration prescriptions, which fail to capture the relativistic fluid response induced by the binary potential. In this work we address this gap by providing the relativistic calculation. We apply standard methods from self-force theory, black hole perturbation theory, and relativistic stellar perturbation theory to compute the relativistic analogue of the spiral density wave and torque-balance results underlying planetary migration. Specifically, we calculate the response of a perfect fluid disc to the perturbing potential of an EMRI, consistently incorporating pressure effects. Using a master enthalpy-like variable and linearised fluid theory, we present a set of proof-of-principle calculations that reconstruct the fluid perturbations and relativistic spiral arm structure for a range of spin values in the Kerr geometry. We derive a relativistic torque-balance equation that enables us to compute and compare local torques with the angular momentum advected through the disc, finding striking agreement when applied to our relativistic disc-EMRI solutions. This opens a promising route towards establishing torque-balance relations between integrated disc torques arising from fluid perturbations and the forces acting on EMRIs embedded in matter.

papers.title: Analyzing Fermionic Dark Matter Scenarios with Anomalous Compact Objects
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider three compact objects (HESS J1731-347, PSR J1231-1411, XTE J1814-338) with anomalous mass-radius relations to analyze the possibility of their being dark matter admixed neutron stars. We try to infer the properties of the dark matter particles, under the assumption of behaving as a free Fermi gas. The main novelty relies on the use of a baryonic equation of state obtained from first principles over the whole density range, which allows the model dependence of the baryonic part of the calculation to be eliminated. Once the possible dark matter admixed neutron star configurations are obtained, we check their stability and whether it is feasible for a neutron star to capture the necessary dark matter fraction. Our analysis shows that our dark matter model favours the dark matter admixed neutron star hypothesis over the pure baryonic neutron star one, with the most favoured dark matter mass of $m_{DM} = 1$~GeV, although the necessary dark matter content cannot be explained in a standard galactic environment.

papers.title: Compensator-Based Inference for Signal Detection Under Unknown Background
papers.abstract: The problem of detecting new signals in the presence of an unknown background is ubiquitous in scientific discoveries and is especially prominent in the physical sciences. Most solutions proposed thus far to address the problem focus on estimating the background distribution and using that estimate to infer the signal. By studying the geometry of the problem, this article demonstrates that estimating the background distribution is somewhat unnecessary for inferring the signal intensity. Instead, it suffices to estimate a single parameter, referred to as the compensator, to account for the incomplete knowledge of the background, substantially reducing the problem's complexity and enabling proper uncertainty propagation. Such a compensator is shown to govern the conservativeness of the inference, both in the proposed setup and in likelihood-based approaches.

papers.title: Shadow and Polarized Images of Schwarzschild-MOG Black Hole Illuminated by Thick Accretion Disk
papers.abstract: Recent EHT polarimetric observations provide a powerful probe of near-horizon physics and modified gravity. We investigate the shadow and polarization images of a static Schwarzschild-MOG black hole illuminated by geometrically thick, optically thin accretion flows. Adopting a phenomenological model and the Hou disk model, and solving null geodesics and relativistic radiative transfer, we study how the MOG parameter, inclination angle, anisotropic synchrotron emission, and flow geometry affect the total intensity and linear polarization. It is found that the MOG parameter mainly enlarges and brightens higher-order photon rings and broadens the shadow, while the inclination angle breaks axial symmetry and enhances polarized emission inside the shadow. The Hou disk model suppresses off-equatorial radiative interference and localizes polarization signals within higher-order rings. Electric vector position angle (EVPA) patterns are mostly azimuthal but vary rapidly near lensed images. These results provide theoretical diagnostics for constraining MOG with EHT/ngEHT polarimetric observations.

papers.title: Making Reconnection Cooler: A relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics model for radiative collisionless reconnection
papers.abstract: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely site for particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has substantially modelled such collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force countering the acceleration of the particles. Here, we systematically derive an energy-momentum sink term in relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription which reproduces the fast reconnection rate seen in kinetic calculations, to model radiative losses. We show that our radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties -- including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the out-flowing plasma -- for inverse Compton cooling applied to two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmarked to kinetic simulations. Our results hold in various cooling regimes with a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory. Our radiative model lays a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, such as in reconnection sites in a local turbulent flow or globally in the magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.

papers.title: To collapse or not to collapse: Halo evolution with self-interacting dark matter mass segregation
papers.abstract: Surprisingly compact substructures in galaxies and galaxy clusters, but also field halos, have been observed by gravitational lensing. They could be difficult to explain with collisionless dark matter (DM). To explain those objects, recent studies focused on the gravothermal collapse that halos consisting of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) can undergo. However, simple models of elastic scattering could face problems explaining those compact objects during very later stages of the collapse and the post-collapse phase, where a black hole may have formed from DM. We aim to explain compact halos while avoiding the gravothermal catastrophe to which typical SIDM models are subject. Therefore, we investigate the evolution of a DM halo for an SIDM model consisting of two species with unequal masses, which features only interactions between the different species but not within themselves. Employing $N$-body simulations, we study the effect of unequal-mass SIDM models on the evolution of an isolated DM halo. In particular, the late stages of its evolution with high central densities are simulated. We find that our two-species SIDM models can produce density cores with their size depending on the mass ratio of the two species. Moreover, mass segregation caused by the unequal particle masses leads to a finite final density state or at least a slowly growing density, which depends on the mass ratio and the mass fraction of the two DM species. SIDM models consisting of two DM species can simultaneously explain DM halos with density cores, as well as systems that are denser in their centre than expected from collisionless DM, while avoiding the gravothermal catastrophe. They are a compelling alternative to single-species models, offering a rich phenomenology.

papers.title: Measurement of femtogauss intergalactic magnetic fields towards Mkn 501
papers.abstract: The intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF) is expected either to be generated via astrophysical processes or to be a relic of phase transitions in the early universe. Upper bounds are set via observations of Faraday rotation measure. Lower bounds have been derived from the non-detection of secondary gamma-rays possibly produced in electromagnetic cascades. We investigate the presence of IGMFs by studying the GeV gamma-ray emission from the nearby blazar Mkn~501 ($z=0.034$), searching for evidence of the extended halo from electromagnetic cascades. We analyse 14 years of data from Fermi-LAT and Swift-XRT/BAT to construct a time-average synchrotron-self Compton model for the TeV spectrum of Mkn~501. This injection spectrum is used to simulate the resulting cascade emission with the ELMAG code for different magnetic field and coherence length configurations. These templates are fit to the Fermi-LAT data to find a best-fitting model for the cascade emission. We find significant ($\ge 5 \sigma$ trial-corrected) evidence of extended secondary emission around Mkn~501, which is consistent with an IGMF with $B_\mathrm{rms}=1.5^{+2.0}_{-1.3}~\mathrm{fG}$ and a coherence length of $\ell_C=10^{+490}_{-5} ~\mathrm{kpc}$ (statistical uncertainties only). When including instrumental systematic uncertainties, the permissible IGMF strength is $B_\mathrm{rms}=1.5^{+8.5}_{-1.1}~\mathrm{fG}$, for fixed $\ell_C=10~\mathrm{kpc}$. The source needs to actively inject TeV gamma-rays for at least 45000 years to match the level of secondary emission. Our results indicate that the secondary gamma-rays are significantly present in the Fermi-LAT data and furthermore, that the effect of plasma-heating by pairs in the cascade appears to be negligible for Mkn~501. The energy spectrum of Mkn~501 favours pair conversion in the intervening low-density intergalactic medium.

papers.title: Strange quark star I: the maximum gravitational mass and deformation of magnetized spinning model
papers.abstract: We investigate the structural parameters of strange quark stars (SQS) under the influence of strong magnetic fields and varying rotational frequencies. The equation of state is computed using the MIT bag model with a density-dependent bag constant and considering the Landau quantization effect regarding the strong magnetic fields up to $5\times10^{17}\,$G in the interior of SQS. Employing the LORENE library, we calculate the structural parameters under different magnetic field strengths and rotational frequencies. Our models are compared in terms of maximum gravitational mass, deformation parameter, binding energy, and compactness. Our equation of state model demonstrates that the gravitational masses are higher than those computed using a MIT bag model with a fixed bag constant. We find the gravitational masses beyond $2.3 \,M_\odot$, which are compatible with the masses of observed compact objects, such as the ``black widow'' pulsar \emph{PSR J0952-0607}, and the \emph{GW190814} event detected by the LIGO/Virgo collaboration. The deformation parameter and maximum gravitational mass of SQS are characterized by fitted functions accounting for variations in both magnetic field strength and rotational frequency. We find the maximum deformation parameter of 1.55 and the maximum gravitational mass of $2.8\, M_\odot$ in the fast-rotating strongly magnetized model.

papers.title: Strange quark star II: the minimal and maximal gravitational mass and the Keplerian configuration
papers.abstract: We employ the MIT bag model with density-dependent bag constant for the equation of state (EOS) to estimate the gravitational mass and Keplerian frequency of rapidly rotating strange quark stars (SQS). In a companion paper we discuss the structural parameters of such rotating stars under the influence of strong magnetic fields. We use the LORENE library to compute the structural parameters at different rotational frequencies in the range of 1100-1300~Hz for a non-magnetized SQS. While there is no minimum limit for the mass of slowly rotating self-bound stars, by computing the maximum rotational frequency, known as the mass-shedding limit, we show that SQS must have a minimum mass to sustain high rotational frequencies. The mass-shedding frequency in our EOS model is lower than that estimated from the MIT bag model EOS with a fixed bag constant. The Keplerian frequency in our model depends linearly on the gravitational mass at the mass-shedding limit (and similarly on the minimum mass) with the slope of 0.08~${\rm kHz}/M_\odot$. We obtain mass limits aligned with the observational data for both the heaviest and the lightest observed pulsars.

papers.title: The Role of Scintillation in Detecting HI Absorption in FRB Spectra
papers.abstract: The 21 cm absorption line of neutral hydrogen has been a long hypothesized observational feature of fast radio burst (FRB) spectra. Difficulties associated with detector noise in extracting HI absorption have been previously studied. We test the role that scintillation plays in its detectability and characterize the regimes where a realistic FRB may yield the 21 cm line. We build an efficient model to simulate diffractive scintillation arising from FRB passage through a thin scattering screen. We find that the absorption profile is detectable in a scintillation-dominated high signal-to-noise spectrum if the scintillation decorrelation bandwidth differs significantly in scale from absorption profile width. Specifically, for a detector with a known SEFD, the HI line can be extracted using a low-pass filter for scintillation bandwidths $< 0.5$ kHz, peak cloud optical depths $> 0.5$, and fluences $\gtrsim$ SEFD Jy ms (assuming a 1 ms duration). Stacking repeat bursts from active repeaters is also useful, but they must be separated in time by more than the diffractive scintillation timescale, otherwise flux modulations with frequency are correlated. By cross-referencing repeating FRB positions with a catalog of Milky Way molecular clouds detected in CO, we find that the sightline to FRB 20180916B may intersect a Galactic molecular cloud. This possibility may be confirmed with a hundred or more baseband-recorded bursts with GBT. We also identify clear observation strategies with FAST and GBT for a range of repeater luminosity functions, with both telescopes needing roughly 500 bursts to confidently detect a peak optical depth of $0.5$.

papers.title: SN 2025aico: Early observations of a faint Type IIb supernova with a low-mass envelope
papers.abstract: We aimed to investigate the physical properties and the underlying explosion mechanisms of the Type IIb SN 2025aico. Through a comprehensive analysis of early-phase optical light curves and spectroscopic data, we aim to constrain the fundamental explosion parameters and evaluate the physical state of the event. We present early multi-band optical imaging and low-resolution optical spectroscopic follow-up observations of the Type IIb SN 2025aico, spanning approximately 70 days from the explosion. We constrain the properties of SN 2025aico by utilizing a hybrid model that combines shock-cooling emission and radioactively powered diffusion, as well as by analyzing the spectroscopic evolution. We use various approaches to constrain the 56Ni mixing from early data, and also compared our spectra with models to constrain the properties of the progenitor. The explosion epoch of SN 2025aico is estimated to be MJD 61032.69, while the rise time in the r_M-band is 22.30 +/- 0.70 days. The peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity in the optical bands is L_opt = (4.07 +/- 0.10) x 10^41 erg/s. The fitting yields a moderate to relatively low 56Ni mass of M_Ni = 0.033 +0.006/-0.004 M_sun and an ejecta mass of M_ej = 2.79 +0.21/-0.18 M_sun. The photospheric velocity near the bolometric peak, measured from the Fe II lambda 5169 line, is 6450 +180/-160 km/s. The derived envelope properties suggest a compact He-star progenitor possessing an H-rich envelope of M_env approx. 0.02 M_sun and a radius of R_env approx. 6-10 R_sun. The derived physical properties of SN 2025aico indicate an origin from a moderate-mass, stripped He-star in a compact binary system, characterized by a minimal residual hydrogen envelope. The explosion itself demonstrates weak to moderate 56Ni mixing throughout the ejecta.
